models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light and benign: under 5 kt through tomorrow, flat water, Pignataro quiet overnight - 06:00 start for Panarea.
briefing.synopsis: The payload carries no pressure or frontal analysis, so I can't give you a chart-level synoptic picture - only the model wind fields. Those show a very weak, essentially gradient-free regime over the archipelago: at Lipari ECMWF IFS/AIFS/ICON-2i (all 04 Oct 00Z) consensus gives 4.0 kt ENE this evening, backing to 2.6 kt NE at midnight and 3.3 kt NW by 06:00 tomorrow, then 3.1 kt WNW at midday. Nothing in the next 24-48 h exceeds about 5 kt mean at any island, with seas running 0.1 ft. The only signal of change is late Tuesday 6 Oct, when Lipari builds to 6.4 kt E by evening - still modest.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Porto Pignataro is the pick for tonight: 3.3 kt NE, gusts 8.2 kt, swell 0.1 ft from NW, all well clear of its exposed 200-250° arc (04 Oct 00Z model consensus). Marina Lunga and Valle Muria score essentially the same, so the choice is about convenience, not shelter. Nothing in the overnight data would push the fleet to move; the only thing worth watching is the wind backing through NE, and Marina Lunga is open on that sector if you end up there.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Lipari to Panarea, 12 nm on 029°T, is light all day - the window opens 06:00 with 3.9 kt NW, gusting 7.6, 0.1 ft seas, close reach, and never tops 4.5 kt through a 14:00 departure. Recommended departure is 06:00, but there is no deterioration flagged at any point in the day, so a later start costs you nothing but sailing breeze. Expect to motor for part of it. Panarea's San Pietro buoy field is the overnight recommendation: 2.0 kt SE, gusts 4.3, swell 0.2 ft NNW - open to the SE but there is no wind in it.

passage_notes.note: 3-5 kt NW-WNW all day, gusts 6.6-9.3 kt, seas 0.1 ft. Close reach early, beam reach after midday. Verdict go on every window; motoring likely.
Same airmass: 3.9-5.5 kt NW-WNW, gusts to 13.6 kt, seas 0.2-0.3 ft. A 06:00 or 08:00 start gives a 4 h beam reach. Berthing is the constraint, not the passage.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (06 Oct, 11 nm, 219°T)
passage_notes.note: 3-6 kt ESE-SE, gusts to 13.0 kt, seas 0.3-0.4 ft. Broad to beam reach, go on all windows.
First real sailing: 5.8 kt SSE at 06:00 building to 8.4 kt ESE by the 14:00 window, gusts to 18.1 kt, seas 0.7-0.9 ft. Broad reach throughout. Filicudi Porto sheltered at 7.9 kt ESE, gusts 14.8.
5-6 kt SSE-ESE, seas 0.7-0.9 ft, close reach early then head-to-wind by midday - motor the back half. Santa Marina Salina sheltered at 3.0 kt SSE.

The one leg with a timing decision. 10.3 kt SW / 2.0 ft at 06:00, building to 16.2 kt W / 3.3 ft by midday and 18.1 kt W / 3.9 ft at 14:00, which trips the caution threshold on sustained wind. Flagged as deteriorating after 11:00 - plan a morning departure.
Portorosa Marina enclosed, all-round shelter, but 11.9 kt W with gusts to 26.8 kt in the forecast - expect a windy approach and plan line handling accordingly.

cautions: Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli is the only option there, is open from every direction and is marked no-anchoring. It rates workable only because 05 Oct is forecast calm (3.2 kt N, gusts 7.2, swell 0.3 ft). Treat the Stromboli option as contingent on that staying true.
Several light-air windows show gust-to-mean ratios near 3:1 (e.g. 12.8 kt against 4.3 kt on today's leg). That is an interval-maximum gust from a single model in near-calm air, not a squall signal.
Salina → Portorosa on 09 Oct is the only caution verdict in the payload - 18.1 kt sustained W, 3.9 ft, on the 14:00 window. That is five days out and worth re-reading nightly.

Light-air direction is unreliable: forecast stability shows mean direction shifts of 37° at 12-24 h lead even though wind-speed shifts average only 0.5 kt. Don't plan a sail-only passage around a specific heading.
